channel.title: BK Reader (The Brooklyn Reader) - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from BK Reader (The Brooklyn Reader) (bkreader.com)

item.title: Brooklyn's Myrtle Avenue Restaurant Week Returns
item.description: Thirteen Fort Greene and Clinton Hill restaurants are serving prix-fixe menus during the fifth annual Myrtle Avenue Restaurant Week, spotlighting the corridor’s diverse global cuisines.

item.title: This Brooklyn High School is Heating Itself With Vegetable Oil Biofuel
item.description: In the basement of Edward R. Murrow High School in Midwood, four boilers power the sprawling school of roughly 4,000 students, according to CBS New York.

item.title: Appeals Court Sides With Democrats in Congressional Redistricting Case That Affects Brooklyn
item.description: In a brief order issued Thursday, five judges on the First Judicial Department’s appellate division said Congressional District 11 can be redrawn. As a result, the redistricting commission must now begin redrawing congressional districts that will affect Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Staten Island, Politico reported.

item.title: Must-Watch Brooklyn Nets Games in the Stretch Run
item.description: With the schedule shrinking and playoffs looming, the Brooklyn Nets move forward fast, needing results while finding room to grow.

item.title: Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump's Tariffs
item.description: In a 6-3 vote, the majority of the U.S. Supreme Court found that the Constitution gives Congress the power to imposes taxes and tariffs. "The Framers did not vest any part of the taxing power in the Executive Branch," Chief Justice John Roberts wrote.

item.title: NYC Students March Toward HBCU Band Dreams
item.description: For one morning in Brooklyn, the road to the South ran straight through a music stand at the third annual NYC HBCU Band Audition Fair in Bedford-Stuyvesant.

item.title: Five New Yorkers Win $5,000 For Improving NYC Life
item.description: The David Prize, an initiative of The Walentas Family Foundation, awarded $5,000 to five New Yorkers who are making a difference in their communities. One Brooklynite is spreading love in Flatbush through basketball.

item.title: Community Board Backs Greenpoint Waterfront Towers
item.description: Community Board 1 recommends approval of Monitor Point, a three-tower waterfront development in Greenpoint, with conditions on affordability, transit and parks.

item.title: Feb 21: Brooklyn Black History Maker, Dr. Susan McKinney Steward
item.description: Raised in Crown Heights, Dr. McKinney Steward was the first Black woman to earn a medical degree in New York.

item.title: NY Governor Allocates $1M for Weeksville Heritage Center
item.description: The state is awarding $1 million for Weeksville to preserve Black heritage and expand community programs.
